title: Thresholded Region Fallback Router for SLO-preserving Multi-region Routing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: production traffic in multi-region deployments sometimes causes regional resource exhaustion or tail-latency spikes that violate customer SLOs. Current steering is proximity-first with hard geo-pinning and blunt shedding, which leads to either unnecessary cross-region latency or large-scale request drops under surge. Goal: implement a thresholded fallback router that preserves SLOs by combining latency-aware routing, soft geo-pinning, and capacity-aware steering with region-level circuit breakers and progressive load-shedding tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Router routes requests by policy (latency+capacity) and falls back to compatible model variants without exceeding configured regional SLOs.
Region circuit breaker trips when regional CPU/GPU utilization and queueing push predicted p99 above SLO threshold; traffic is gradually shed and rerouted per policy.
Soft geo-pinning maintained for stable sessions (pin score) but relaxed for SLO preservation using jittered soft-release windows.
Canary rollout demonstrates no >5% increase in p99 latency and <1% additional error rate compared to baseline after 48h.
Operational dashboards and alerts (p95/p99 latency, drop rate, circuit-breaker events) created and validated.
End-to-end tests simulate regional overload and verify progressive fallback, KV cache affinity best-effort, and graceful degradation of large batch requests.
design_notes: Router computes a dynamic score per candidate region: score = w_lat * est_latency + w_util * util_penalty + w_pin * pin_penalty. We will tune weights per customer tier.
Capacity-aware steering uses a token-bucket per-region representing headroom for synthetic and production traffic; when tokens deplete, router prefers fallbacks or model-quantized variants.
Circuit breaker state machine: CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN (probabilistic shed + probe) -> OPEN (redirect majority of traffic) -> COOLDOWN -> CLOSED. Probing cadence exponential backoff.

Soft geo-pinning: keep a lightweight pin score that decays over time; thresholded release when region score drops below soft_release_threshold for N minutes. Pinning respects KV cache locality hints to avoid cache thrashing.

Load-shedding tiers: Tier A (best-effort cheap responses): apply 10% shed; Tier B (latency-sensitive): prefer model fallbacks; Tier C (bulk/batch): defer or reject with structured retry-after metadata.
Compatibility matrix to map requests to model variants during fallback (same quality buckets), stored in config service with versioning.
Telemetry surface includes decision reasoning (scores, tokens consumed, circuit-breaker reasons) for tracing and postmortems.
decisions: Use probabilistic shedding during SOFT_OPEN to avoid thundering herd during recovery.
Expose weight knobs for latency vs capacity in the router config; default balances toward SLO-preservation for P0 customers.
Fallbacks will prefer model-quantized variants that maintain API compatibility rather than downgrading tokenization or response format.
Integrate with existing autoscaler signals but keep router control-loop separate to avoid cascading scaling churn.
tradeoffs: Stronger capacity weighting reduces cross-region latency gains but avoids SLO violations — short-term customer latency may increase for long-term reliability.
Soft pin decay improves global throughput but increases cache miss rates; mitigated by preserving pin for golden-cached prefixes.
Adding more decision telemetry increases storage and trace cardinality; we limit sampling rate to 1% for full decision traces and log aggregated metrics at 100%.
Probabilistic shedding can cause non-determinism in customer experiences; we document behavior in SLA notes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring function, token-bucket logic, and circuit-breaker state transitions.
Integration harness that replays production traces with simulated regional capacity constraints and asserts SLO compliance.
Chaos test: randomized region outages and delayed probes to validate safe fallback and rejoin behavior.
Canary in region: start at 1% traffic for low-risk customers, escalate to 10% then 50% if no regressions for 24h intervals.
Load tests with mixed request profiles (chat, completion, embeddings) to validate tiered shedding behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'threshold-fallback' for internal test orgs only.
Phase 1: Canary 1% for a controlled set of customers in eu-west and us-east for 48h.
Phase 2: Expand to 10% with alerting thresholds tightened; monitor p99, error rate, shed rate, and cb events.
Phase 3: Global enable for non-enterprise tenants; enterprise customers opt-in with per-tenant thresholds.
Rollback: global kill switch that reverts to prior proximity-first steering and reuses prior capacity signals.
metrics: regional utilization (GPU and CPU), queue length, request concurrency
circuit-breaker state change count and duration
shed rate by tier and by region
cross-region hop rate (percentage of requests routed away from nearest region)
successful fallback rate (requests served by fallback variant vs failures)
user-visible error rate and retry-after responses
implementation_todos: Add router scoring module and configuration API
Implement per-region token-buckets and lease bookkeeping
Circuit-breaker FSM with probe scheduler and metrics hooks
KV cache hint propagation and pin-score telemetry
Fallback model variant lookup and compatibility checks
Dashboard panels and alert rules (Grafana + SLO alerting)
E2E tests: trace-based harness and chaos tests
Documentation: operator runbook and public API behavior note
